prose.favour: The case in its favour rests mostly on growth: profit grew 315% compared with a year earlier. Also in its favour: sales grew 119% compared with a year earlier; profit covers interest costs 4.0 times over; and debt is lower than shareholders' equity (debt-to-equity 0.67). Other areas on this side: the balance sheet, the recent price trend, what the price implies.
prose.against: The case against rests mostly on cash flow and the balance sheet: free cash flow for the last financial year was negative: the business spent more than it generated. Also against it: profit shrank 15.2% a year on average over three years; the 3-year maximum drawdown was -50.0%, a deep fall; and one-year volatility is 44.5%, high. Other areas on this side: price behaviour, risk, growth.
prose.weighing: Weighing them: 7 points in favour and 7 against give an even split. The pool score is 40 of 100. The side that carries most weight is growth. That gives an educational rating of Hold with high confidence. This is a rule-based reading of the evidence above, not a prediction.
